question: A contract-review tool extracts a governing_law field indicating which jurisdiction's law applies to a contract. In practice, some contracts state this explicitly, some imply it ambiguously across two jurisdictions, and some never mention it at all. The current enum only lists specific jurisdiction names, forcing the model to guess in ambiguous cases. How should the schema be revised?
options: A) Change governing_law to a boolean field indicating only whether any jurisdiction is mentioned in the contract text
B) Add an "unclear" enum value to distinguish genuinely ambiguous or unstated cases from confidently identified jurisdictions
C) Set tool_choice to {"type": "any"} so the model is forced to pick a jurisdiction value from the enum on every single contract
D) Duplicate every jurisdiction name in the enum with an "ambiguous_" prefix so each jurisdiction has an ambiguous counterpart value
correct_answers: B) Add an "unclear" enum value to distinguish genuinely ambiguous or unstated cases from confidently identified jurisdictions
explanations: Collapsing the field to a boolean throws away the actual jurisdiction information for the majority of contracts where it is clearly stated, losing valuable structured data.

Correct. Adding an explicit "unclear" enum value gives the model a truthful, structured way to represent ambiguous or unstated cases instead of being forced into a specific jurisdiction it can't confidently determine.
tool_choice controls whether a tool is invoked at all, not the permissible values within an already-defined field's enum, so it doesn't address the ambiguous-value problem.
Doubling every enum value with an ambiguous variant bloats the schema unnecessarily and still doesn't cover contracts where no jurisdiction is mentioned at all.
